name: Open Data Directive (PSI)
evidence_rating: thin: large ex-ante forecasts and self-reported maturity scores; no ex-post evaluation of the Directive yet; causal evidence on open data exists only outside the EU
summary: The Commission forecast that the Open Data Directive would make public data worth about EUR 194 billion a year by 2028 and support around 709,000 jobs, but none of these forecasts has been checked: the evaluation due from 2025 had not been published by October 2026. Monitoring relies on countries' self-assessed open data maturity, which reached 86% in 2025, with the lowest score for demonstrating impact. Research from outside the EU shows free public data can spur discoveries and new entrants, but no study measures what this Directive has achieved.

indicators.objective: The 2018 recast proposal has no LFS indicators; the memorandum says impact will be monitored through the European Data Portal's annual Open Data Maturity 'landscaping' and an evaluation no sooner than 17 July 2025 (Art. 18). No such evaluation had been published by October 2026
Availability and re-use of public sector data
indicators.evidence: Measured: EU-27 average maturity 86% in 2025 (+3 pp on 2024); policy 93%, portal 85%, quality 83%; the 'impact' dimension is least mature at 82%. Self-assessment questionnaire filled in by national administrations, so it tracks activity rather than economic effect.

indicators.objective: Economic value of public sector data
indicators.indicator: Direct economic value of PSI EUR 194bn in 2028 (preferred option) vs EUR 150bn baseline and EUR 52bn in 2018
indicators.evidence: Not measured against the forecast. A Commission-funded market study estimated the EU open data market at EUR 184bn in 2019 with a 2025 forecast of EUR 200-334bn, but it uses different definitions and cannot attribute value to the Directive.

indicators.indicator: 709,000 persons employed in PSI-based activities by 2028 (vs 518,000 baseline)
Cost of making PSI available falls to EUR 2.7-3bn (vs EUR 3.8-4.1bn baseline)
Direct effect of HVDs EUR 75bn in 2028 (+EUR 6bn vs baseline); indirect EUR 201bn
indicators.evidence: HVD Regulation (EU) 2023/138 applicable since June 2024; Open Data Maturity 2025 reports implementation ongoing. No impact measurement yet.

literature.citation: European Commission (2018), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Directive on the re-use of public sector information (executive summary SWD(2018) 128), SWD(2018) 127
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Directive on the re-use of public sector information (executive summary SWD(2018) 128)
literature.headline: Direct economic value of PSI EUR 52bn in 2018; preferred option lifts it to about EUR 194bn in 2028 (30% above EUR 150bn baseline); jobs 709,000 vs 518,000; cost of opening data EUR 2.7bn vs 4.1bn baseline
literature.summary_plain: The Commission forecast that the recast would make public data worth about EUR 194 billion a year to the economy by 2028, 30% more than without it, and support about 190,000 extra jobs.

literature.citation: European Commission (2018), Evaluation of Directive 2003/98/EC on the re-use of public sector information (executive summary SWD(2018) 129), SWD(2018) 145
literature.title: Evaluation of Directive 2003/98/EC on the re-use of public sector information (executive summary SWD(2018) 129)
literature.method: review (Deloitte study, Open Data Maturity report, consultations)
literature.outcomes: competition; jobs and services; cross-border re-use
literature.headline: PSI Directive effective in ensuring fairer competition and enabling new jobs and services, less so for cross-border re-use; positive cost-benefit balance; challenges remain on dynamic data, charging above marginal cost, data lock-in
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's evaluation of the earlier PSI rules found they helped create services and jobs but that real-time data and high fees were still holding re-use back.

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), Impact assessment report accompanying the Implementing Regulation laying down a list of specific high-value datasets (executive summary SWD(2022) 433), SWD(2022) 432
literature.title: Impact assessment report accompanying the Implementing Regulation laying down a list of specific high-value datasets (executive summary SWD(2022) 433)
literature.headline: Direct effect of preferred option EUR 75bn in 2028, EUR 6bn above baseline; indirect forward effect EUR 201bn (EUR 16bn above baseline); figures described as estimates as dataset value is hard to isolate
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected free, API-based access to key public datasets to add about EUR 6 billion a year in direct value by 2028.

literature.citation: data.europa.eu (European Commission) (2025), Open Data Maturity Report 2025, data.europa.eu
literature.title: Open Data Maturity Report 2025
literature.headline: EU-27 average maturity 86% in 2025 (+3 pp); impact dimension least mature at 82%; HVD implementation ongoing
literature.summary_plain: Countries rate their open data policies and portals highly (86% on average), but score lowest on showing actual impact.

literature.citation: European Data Portal (Capgemini Invent et al.) (2020), The Economic Impact of Open Data: Opportunities for value creation in Europe, European Data Portal study for the European Commission
literature.authors: European Data Portal (Capgemini Invent et al.)
literature.title: The Economic Impact of Open Data: Opportunities for value creation in Europe
literature.venue: European Data Portal study for the European Commission
literature.headline: Open data market size estimated at EUR 184bn (2019), forecast EUR 199.5-334.2bn in 2025
literature.summary_plain: A Commission-funded study put the value of Europe's open data market at EUR 184 billion in 2019, but did not test what the Directive itself contributed.
literature.quality: modelled estimate; no attribution to the Directive

literature.citation: Nagaraj (2022), The Private Impact of Public Data: Landsat Satellite Maps Increased Gold Discoveries and Encouraged Entry, Management Science 68(1), 564-582
literature.title: The Private Impact of Public Data: Landsat Satellite Maps Increased Gold Discoveries and Encouraged Entry
literature.method: causal: quasi-experiment using timing and cloud-cover variation in Landsat coverage
literature.headline: Free public satellite data nearly doubled the rate of significant gold discoveries in newly mapped regions and raised new entrants' share of discoveries from about 10% to 25%
literature.summary_plain: When the US released free satellite maps, gold discoveries nearly doubled and newcomers found a much bigger share - evidence that opening public data can boost competition, though not a test of the EU Directive.
literature.period_geography: global gold exploration, US data release
literature.quality: not EU-specific; indirect evidence for the Directive's logic
